scope.completionUnit: geography scope x explicit value-chain coverage unit x analytical domain
scope.rule: A Nordic claim must declare represented and missing geographies. Norway is never a proxy for Nordic coverage. Political-Nordic and overlapping Indigenous coverage are separate aggregation classes and must never be added together as independent territory.

classes.label: Political-Nordic reporting scopes
classes.definition: The eight mandatory political reporting scopes. Their administrative containment means they are not automatically additive; source-specific territorial boundaries must be reconciled before totals are calculated.

classes.label: Overlapping Sápmi scope
classes.definition: A cross-border Indigenous scope that overlaps political reporting scopes and is assessed separately for knowledge completeness, rights-holder participation and interpretation.

classes.label: Context-only geography
classes.definition: A contextual region or external geography used for dependencies and comparisons, not a Nordic political completion unit.

aggregationModel.antiDoubleCountRule: Never sum cells across aggregation classes. Within the political class, reconcile state and autonomous-territory source boundaries before aggregation; Sápmi remains a non-additive overlapping lens.

geographies.definition: Aggregate Nordic political region; use only with explicit represented and missing member geographies and a reconciled territorial boundary method.
geographies.antiDoubleCountRule: Do not combine this aggregate reference with any member cell.

geographies.definition: The Danish political reporting scope; Greenland and the Faroe Islands are assessed separately for food-system coverage.
geographies.antiDoubleCountRule: When Faroe Islands or Greenland cells are included, the Denmark source boundary must exclude or otherwise reconcile those territories before addition.

geographies.definition: The Finnish political reporting scope; Åland is assessed separately for food-system coverage.
geographies.antiDoubleCountRule: When Åland cells are included, the Finland source boundary must exclude or otherwise reconcile Åland before addition.

geographies.definition: Self-governing territory in the Kingdom of Denmark, assessed as its own food-system geography.
Self-governing territory in the Kingdom of Denmark, assessed as its own food-system geography.
Autonomous region of Finland, assessed as its own food-system geography.
Cross-border Indigenous geography overlapping Norway, Sweden, Finland and the Kola Peninsula; requires a rights-holder and human-evidence route.
geographies.antiDoubleCountRule: Assess separately for completeness and rights-holder interpretation; never add Sápmi cells to political-Nordic totals.

geographies.definition: Contextual Arctic region used for climate, marine, logistics, livelihood and dependency analysis; not a Nordic political completion unit.
Contextual Baltic Sea region used for marine, trade, environmental and regulatory dependencies; not a Nordic political completion unit.
Contextual northwestern-Russian part of the cross-border Sápmi geography; it is not a Nordic political unit.
European Union policy, market and regulatory context affecting Nordic food systems.
European Economic Area context affecting Nordic food systems.
Countries and regions outside the Nordic political geography when a more specific geography is not yet registered.
Global system context and dependencies that cannot be represented by one external geography.

geographyLevels.definition: Aggregate regional level covering the Nordic political geography.
County, province or comparable statistical/administrative region.
Specific farm, factory, port, kitchen, store or other facility.
Sea, coastal zone, fisheries management area or marine ecosystem.
Origin-destination corridor used to analyze trade and logistics dependencies.

Seeds, feed, fertilizer, energy, equipment, technology, finance and other supplied inputs.
Production or harvest of biological food resources.
Cultivation of field crops and arable food/feed crops.
Breeding and husbandry of domesticated livestock for food.
Production of vegetables, fruit, berries, herbs and protected crops.
Wild capture of aquatic food resources.
Farming of fish, shellfish, algae and other aquatic organisms.
Reindeer husbandry as livelihood, food production and cultural system.
Gathering, hunting and harvesting of terrestrial wild foods.
Transformation of primary outputs into ingredients and food products.
Slaughter, landing, milling, grading, cooling and other first transformations.
Manufacture of food and beverage products.
Production of food, feed or functional ingredients used in further processing.
Packaging production, filling and packing operations associated with food products.
Storage, transport and wholesale movement between production, markets and users.
Warehousing, silos, controlled storage and inventory holding.
Physical transport, routing and logistics coordination.
Temperature-controlled storage and transport.
Wholesale aggregation, brokerage and distribution.
Commercial and public channels through which food is procured or sold to final users.
Physical and digital retail sale of food to households.
Hotels, restaurants, catering and commercial meal service.
Public purchasing and contracting of food and meal services.
Farm shops, markets, community-supported agriculture and direct digital channels.
Redistribution of surplus or donated food for consumption.
Preparation, eating and dietary use by final consumers.
Food acquisition, preparation and consumption in households.
Meals served through schools, health care, care institutions, defence and other public services.
Meals consumed through commercial food-service channels.
Collection, recovery, recycling and disposal after loss, surplus or use.
Points where edible or inedible food-system material becomes loss, surplus or waste.
Collection, separation, sorting and preprocessing of return flows.
Recovery into materials, products or ingredients without biological treatment.
Composting, digestion, fermentation and other biological recovery.
Return of nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, carbon or organic matter to productive soils or systems.
Energy recovery from food-system residues or waste.
Incineration without useful recovery, landfill, discharge or other terminal treatment.

domains.definition: System purpose, boundary, units, feedbacks, assumptions and functional relationships.
Costs, revenues, margins, profitability, finance and distribution of economic value.
Concentration, entry, rivalry, bargaining and competitive conditions.
Ownership, decision rights, contracts, agenda-setting and structural power.
Laws, policies, institutions, implementation and accountability.
Trade flows, external dependencies, domestic capacity and self-sufficiency methods.
Availability, access, utilization, stability, shock response and adaptive capacity.
Prevention, cascading use, recovery, recirculation, loss and waste outcomes.
Facilities, networks, equipment, storage, logistics and operational capacity.
Availability, marketing, convenience, choice architecture, practices and consumption behaviour.
Greenhouse-gas emissions, sequestration, climate risk, adaptation and mitigation.
Land use, soil condition, soil carbon, erosion, contamination and productive capacity.
Water use, availability, quality, runoff and catchment impacts.
Species, habitats, genetic diversity and ecosystem functions affected by food systems.
Marine ecosystems, stocks, seabed, coastal impacts and eutrophication.
Diet quality, nutritional adequacy, disease burden and healthy sustainable diets.

domains.labelEn: Food safety, One Health and biosecurity
domains.definition: Food hazards, zoonoses, antimicrobial resistance, traceability, surveillance and biosecurity.
Animal health, welfare conditions, mortality, disease and husbandry impacts.
Employment, labor supply, skills, safety, bargaining and working conditions.
Distributional outcomes, affordability, inclusion, rights and procedural justice.

domains.labelEn: Indigenous rights, culture and food sovereignty
domains.definition: Indigenous rights, knowledge, livelihoods, cultural continuity and authority over food systems.
Research, innovation, adoption, infrastructure change and transition pathways.
Data quality, methods, comparability, provenance, uncertainty and knowledge gaps.

outcomes.definition: Sufficient food supply is physically available.
People can economically and physically obtain appropriate food.
Food supports adequate nutrition and health when consumed.
Food-system functions persist or recover through shocks and long-term change.
Food-borne hazards and health risks are prevented or controlled.
Dietary patterns support health while respecting environmental and social constraints.
Resources retain value and cycle at high utility with reduced virgin input and loss.
Economic value is created through food-system activity.
Actors and activities remain economically viable under defined conditions.
Food-system work provides safe, fair and sustainable livelihoods.
Food systems sustain viable rural, island and coastal communities.
Economic value, costs and risks are distributed fairly across actors.
Benefits, burdens, voice and rights are distributed justly.
Communities retain food-related culture, knowledge, rights and decision authority.
Emissions fall and systems adapt to climate risk.
Soils maintain biological, physical and chemical functions.
Water remains clean and available for ecosystems, people and production.
Food-system air pollutants and harmful exposure are reduced.
Species, habitats and ecosystem functions are maintained or restored.
Marine and coastal ecosystems retain structure, function and resilience.
Animals experience good health and welfare under defined standards.
The system can develop, evaluate, adopt and scale appropriate innovations.
Institutions coordinate, implement, learn and remain accountable.

Harvests terrestrial wild foods.

Transports or coordinates food-system goods.
Operates storage, terminal or distribution infrastructure.
Aggregates and wholesales food or inputs.
Sells food to final consumers.
Operates commercial meal or catering services.
Operates kitchens and meal services in public institutions.
Operates direct-sale channels between producers and consumers.
Collects and redistributes surplus food for consumption.
Collects and sorts food-system waste or residues.
Recovers materials or products from return flows.
Recovers and returns nutrients or organic matter.
Recovers energy from food-system residues.
Performs terminal disposal or discharge.
Holds ownership or parent-company control.
Owns critical physical food-system infrastructure.
Provides labor within the food system.
Acquires, prepares and consumes food.
Provides banking, credit or other financial services.
Supplies risk capital or holds investment interests.
Provides insurance or transfers food-system risk.
Develops or supplies food-system technologies.
Collects, controls or supplies food-system data.
Defines, verifies or certifies standards and labels.
National political or executive authority.
Subnational political or administrative authority.

Non-governmental, community or advocacy organization.
Produces public information, scrutiny or narratives about food systems.

Feed material for terrestrial or aquatic animals.
Living biological material other than registered genetic material.
Seeds, breeding stock, gametes or other reproductive material.
Co-product or residual material retaining potential use.
Food leaving the human food chain before retail or consumption under the declared method.
Food waste as defined by the cited measurement method.
Packaging material associated with food-system products.
Nitrogen mass flow.
Phosphorus mass flow.
Potassium mass flow.
Water withdrawal, consumption, discharge or embodied flow.
Energy carrier or quantified energy use/production.
Carbon stock or flow in soils.
Greenhouse-gas emissions or removals.
Non-GHG pollutant emitted to air.
Nutrient, chemical or biological pollutant entering water.
Material or functional ecosystem contribution to the food system.
Payment or revenue between actors.
Cost incurred by an actor or stage.
Observed or transmitted price information affecting decisions.
Margin, mark-up or value-added allocation.
Public subsidy or support payment.

Dry beans, peas, lentils and related pulses.
Potatoes and other edible roots and tubers.
Sugar crops, sugar and caloric sweeteners.
Edible nuts and seeds excluding oilseed-only classification.
Food products originating from terrestrial animals.
Sheep and goat meat or milk products.
Reindeer and wild game food products.
Food from marine and freshwater organisms.
Food products combining or substantially transforming raw commodities.

Novel or alternative protein products and ingredients.

Pasture, hay, silage and other forage.

materialGroups.definition: Non-food seed, breeding or genetic input material.
Mineral nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium or compound fertilizer.
Sewage or industrial sludge relevant to food-system nutrient flows.

circularStrategies.definition: Avoid the need for a resource, product or surplus before it enters the system.
Change use patterns or business models to intensify use and prevent loss.
Use fewer resources or generate less loss per delivered function.
Use a product again in the same form or function, including edible redistribution.
Maintain or repair equipment and infrastructure to extend useful life.
Restore or upgrade equipment and infrastructure for continued use.
Use recovered components or side streams to create a product with the same or comparable function.
Use a recovered product or material in a different function.
Process materials into secondary raw material, soil amendment or nutrient product.
Recover energy while the material is no longer available at its original utility.

A household as an economic and consumption unit.
A physical site or infrastructure asset.

tradeDirections.definition: Origin and destination are within the assessed geography.
A commodity or material enters the assessed geography.
A commodity or material leaves the assessed geography.
An imported commodity or material is exported again under the cited method.
A commodity or material passes through without entering domestic use under the cited method.

A geographic or spatial knowledge object.
A facility, asset or network supporting food-system functions.
A transformation or activity in the food system.
A physical, economic, control, information or human transfer.
A precise factual or analytical proposition with evidence state.
A measured, recorded or directly observed state.
A defined metric used to monitor a system property or outcome.
A versioned collection of observations or records.
A source identity and provenance record, not a duplicate of raw evidence.
A bounded intervention, organization, failure, transition or observed example.
A law, policy, programme, standard or governance instrument.
A dated event affecting food-system state or interpretation.
A conditional future or shock scenario, never an observed fact.
A durable research or decision question.
A precise unknown, blocker or measurement gap with closure route.
A compiled explanation resolving to claims and sources.

crossCuttingLenses.definition: What is included, excluded and used as the functional boundary.
Geographic representation, scale and missing places.
Period, validity, trend and temporal comparison.
Position and transitions in the value chain.
Actor role, bargaining position, ownership and control.
Flow direction, quantity, circular strategy, cascade level and realized outcome.
Source, method, uncertainty, contradiction and readiness.
Distribution of value, costs, risks, voice and rights.
Exposure, vulnerability, response, recovery and adaptation.
Intended, observed and unintended outcomes and trade-offs.

legacyFields.labelEn: The whole food system – boundaries and relationships
legacyFields.definition: Tracked Obsidian field 1; retained exactly as a mixed navigation and migration view, not as a canonical atomic category.
Tracked Obsidian field 2; retained exactly as a mixed navigation and migration view.
Tracked Obsidian field 3; expands to explicit production coverage units rather than the non-coverage parent stage.
Tracked Obsidian field 4; expands to explicit processing coverage units rather than the non-coverage parent stage.
Tracked Obsidian field 5; expands to distribution functions and the direct-sales channel used for local-chain navigation.

legacyFields.labelNb: Handel, servering, offentlige innkjøp og forbruk
legacyFields.labelEn: Retail, food service, public procurement and consumption
legacyFields.definition: Tracked Obsidian field 6; expands across distinct market, procurement and consumption coverage units.
Tracked Obsidian field 7; retained exactly as a multi-domain navigation view.

legacyFields.labelEn: Circularity, food waste, side streams and N-P-K
legacyFields.definition: Tracked Obsidian field 8; expands to explicit return-flow functions, redistribution, circular strategies, physical flows and circularity outcomes.

legacyFields.labelEn: Imports, self-sufficiency, food security and preparedness
legacyFields.definition: Tracked Obsidian field 9; retained exactly as a trade, sufficiency, security and resilience view.

legacyFields.labelNb: Jord, naturmangfold, klima, helse og tilstrekkelighet
legacyFields.labelEn: Soil, biodiversity, climate, health and sufficiency
legacyFields.definition: Tracked Obsidian field 10; expands across environmental condition, health, safety, welfare and food-security facets rather than a four-domain shorthand.
Tracked Obsidian field 11; expands to innovation, infrastructure, alternative-protein macro classes, cases and maturity states.
Tracked Obsidian field 12; expands to political-Nordic and separately overlapping Sápmi candidates with governance facets and anti-double-count review.

legacyFields.labelEn: Methods, evidence, citability and knowledge gaps
legacyFields.definition: Tracked Obsidian field 13; expands to evidence objects and the status facets needed to distinguish discovery, verification, citation readiness, confidence and gap routing.

commodityGroups.rule: Tier-1 macro navigation classes; do not infer commodity-level completeness from coverage of a macro class.

materialGroups.rule: Tier-1 macro navigation classes; process-specific materials and chemical species require lower-tier extensions.

coverageProfiles.label: Canonical political-Nordic macro planning matrix
coverageProfiles.purpose: Expose a tier-1 planning surface across eight political reporting scopes, explicit stage coverage units and analytical domains. Stage units include ordered stages, cross-stage capabilities, contexts and events; they are not a mutually exclusive atomic-leaf partition.

coverageProfiles.label: Canonical overlapping-Sápmi macro planning matrix
coverageProfiles.purpose: Expose the same tier-1 planning surface for the separately assessed, non-additive Sápmi scope. Stage units include ordered stages, cross-stage capabilities, contexts and events; they are not a mutually exclusive atomic-leaf partition, and results must never be added to political-Nordic totals.

coverageProfiles.label: Legacy thirteen-field political-Nordic scope inventory
coverageProfiles.purpose: Create neutral scope events for the tracked thirteen mixed navigation fields across the eight political reporting scopes. A field cell is a navigation/inventory unit, not proof of subject coverage or an atomic ontology leaf.

coverageProfiles.label: Legacy thirteen-field overlapping-Sápmi scope inventory
coverageProfiles.purpose: Create thirteen neutral scope events for the separately assessed, non-additive Sápmi navigation view. A field cell is neither proof of subject coverage nor an atomic ontology leaf, and it must never be added to political-Nordic totals.
